external_relations.target_title: skill(devops): author capacity-reclaim — third materialization of the devops-sre role, sibling to sre-triage and deploy-monitor

source.description:
## PROBLEM

dev/core has no permission normalisation target. Verified 2026-08-05 during xtrm-gvek4: `.xtrm/skills/default/capacity-reclaim/SKILL.md` landed mode 0600 in the orchestrator's checkout while `sre-triage` and `deploy-monitor` were 0664, and the orchestrator normalised it by hand post-merge.

Root cause is rule 10 of the skill the bead produced: git tracks only the executable bit, so a file's read mode is set by the umask of the shell that checks it out. The authoring `chmod 644` was a no-op on what git delivers. In the authoring worktree all three sibling skills read 0600, which confirms the mode is a property of the checkout, not of the repo.

The fault only hits files NEW to a given checkout — files already present keep their existing mode — which is why the tree looks correct until something new arrives.

## SCOPE

Add a repo target (npm script and/or Makefile rule) that normalises xtrm-managed asset modes to the tree convention (0664 files, 0775 dirs) after checkout, pull, or `xt update --apply`.

Rule 11 from the same skill applies directly and is the main design constraint: the normaliser must cover the WHOLE asset tree, not the subset that failed first. `make alert-perms` in mercury/infra covered `prometheus/alerts/*.yml` only and silently did not cover `prometheus.yml`, `web.yml` or `alertmanager.yml` — a remediation narrower in scope than the fault it remediates. Do not repeat that shape here.

Rule 12 also applies: a target that must be run by hand is detection without disarming the producer. Consider wiring it to the operations that create the fault (post-merge/post-checkout hook, or the tail of `xt update --apply`) rather than leaving it as a command an operator must remember.

## NON_GOALS

Do not change any skill's content. Do not attempt to make git carry the mode — it cannot.

## VALIDATION

After a fresh clone or pull under `umask 077`, running the target leaves every xtrm-managed asset at the tree convention, and a check target fails when it does not.
source.notes: Context from xt-end close of xtrm-gvek4: repo-wide worktree debt observed but NOT actioned (outside contract) — restart-audit reports 46 branch-without-worktree, 17 closed-pr-branch, 1 orphaned-managed-dir under xt/; branch-gc dry-run would delete 17 merged/closed branches. Separate hygiene concern from this bead's permission target; flagged for the operator, not filed as work.
